Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

multiCSN (development version)

  • fix: Validate scores, binary labels, and top-k budgets in ranking_metrics() before computing metrics.
  • breaking: Use inferCSN::deletion_rank_weight() in place of multiCSN::network_ordinal_weight().

multiCSN 0.1.0

  • The independent layered workflow has an explicit input and result contract. Candidate preparation and fitting require one joined data layer per assay; per-group normalization also requires one joined counts layer.

  • Candidate preparation rebuilds the multiCSN catalogue. In-memory fitting returns the complete scientific tables without storing a Seurat object by default.

  • Fitting returns valid empty endpoint tables when the peak detection threshold removes every candidate region.

  • Constant TF expression produces empty TF layers with explicit accounting; the independent region-gene layer is retained.

  • Checkpoint hashes use SHA-256 through digest, retaining support for R 4.1.

  • Explicit peak separators are respected when normalizing chromatin assays, and normalized values remain aligned when peak names are canonicalized.

  • Boolean endpoint validation returns FALSE for malformed result files and invalid summary counts.

  • Require inferCSN 1.2.6 for the shared deletion-evidence ranking API.

  • prepare_candidates() builds the unfiltered candidate catalogue and motif matches in one call; find_motifs() uses the bundled motifs and motif2tf by default.

  • fit_layered_network() gains preset = c("state", "timepoint") for the two common fitting designs and output_dir to write the network tables after a complete fit. Use checkpoint_dir to retain resumable checkpoints.

  • validate_network_endpoints() checks a saved result directory; read_network_endpoints() detects the file format and can return a single table; classify_edge_transitions() labels the state transition.

  • New evaluation helpers: evaluate_network(), ranking_metrics(), tie_aware_auroc(), tie_aware_average_precision(), expected_precision_at_k(), signed_ordinal_weight(), as_edge_table() and weight_matrix_to_edges().

  • Peak coordinate parsing no longer calls the deprecated Signac StringToGRanges() and GRangesToString().

  • create_seurat_object() works with current Signac annotation checks.

  • Removed define_states_new(), assign_genes_to_states_new1() and assign_genes_to_states_simple(), which duplicated define_states() and assign_genes_to_states(), and JI_across_topregs() and biglist_compute_betweenness_degree(), which failed on every call.

  • Removed arguments that had no effect: lag_fraction and lag_steps from the Network and Seurat methods of inferCSN(), pseudotime from the Network method and seed from the Seurat method; the per-method arguments of the fit_models() generic; label_points, max_overlaps and grid_n from plotPerturbation(); weight_cutoff and compare_random from plot_gene_rank() for Seurat objects; group.by from plot_rewiring() and plot_state_rewiring(); celltypes from metrics() for Network; method from compute_JI_topregs(); directed from compute_pagerank(); assay from get_pseudotime() for Seurat.

  • fit_models() passes extend to the GREAT peak-to-gene mapping.

  • Fewer hard dependencies: ComplexHeatmap, circlize, thisplot, tidygraph, ggraph, ggnetwork, patchwork and rlang move to Suggests and are needed only by the plotting functions. Optional packages are installed on first use through thisutils::check_r(strict = TRUE) (thisutils >= 0.5.4), which stops only if installation fails; purrr is no longer used.

multiCSN 0.0.1

  • Trajectory partitions, gene assignments, subnetworks, and heatmap annotations now use state terminology consistently, with default IDs such as state_1. Existing saved assignments are normalized when read by the new interfaces.

  • Initial release.

  • Removed the unused dynamic_genes and dynamic_genes_new interfaces, their legacy GAM implementation, and the gam dependency. Use scop::RunDynamicFeatures directly; state inference already uses this path.

  • XGBoost fitting uses xgb.train with DMatrix input and maps nthread = -1 to the native all-thread setting, avoiding removed high-level API arguments.
